Leicester City Target Former Championship Goalkeeper

  • Championship, EFL, League One, Transfer News
  • Kyle Kennealey
  • Leicester City, Preston North End
  • September 17, 2026
  • 1:29 pm
  • No Comments
Facebook
Twitter
LinkedIn
Pinterest

WhatsApp

Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:07
Instaread

Leicester City are looking to strengthen their goalkeeping department with the addition of experienced goalkeeper David Cornell. 

The Foxes have endured a hugely underwhelming return to League One following last season’s relegation, with defensive issues remaining a cause for concern.

Hart: City performance 'exceptional' against United they'll push Arsenal for title
'It's football' - Maresca reacts to Manchester derby goal error
‘It’s been chastening to say the least’ – Should Burnley be worried?
Wrexham might have different expectations after West Ham ‘reality check’
‘This should be a feisty affair’ - Essential EFL previews Wolves vs West Brom
A look at the ‘life-affirming and frightening’ fixture of Millwall vs West Ham
'We have to believe in the team' - Lampard focused on Coventry turnaround
Which five players could make their England return?
Sage underlines importance of Henderson's new contract
Does Alexander Isak get star struck? Liverpool star fact checks the internet!
'Not on my radar' - Carrick dismisses speculation on Man Utd future
Tuchel names first England squad since World Cup - The Verdict

According to Pete O’Rourke, Leicester have opened talks with the 35-year-old, who left Championship side Preston North End this summer.

What Would Cornell Bring?

Making a move for a goalkeeper outside the transfer window is hardly ideal for any club, never mind a team like Leicester who are currently in the limelight for a variety of reasons. With experience and know-how needed in abundance, Welshman Cornell would help to bring that. Having begun his career with Swansea City, he featured in the Scottish Premiership with St Mirren, after a loan in his home country’s top division at Port Talbot Town.

ADVERTISEMENT

Since then, Cornell got a full season of League Two action under his belt at Northampton Town in the 2018/19 campaign. After adding a further 34 appearances the following season, his action on the pitch has been few and far between this decade. A third-tier loan with Ipswich Town added 15 matches in the lockdown campaign, before featuring on 30 occasions for Peterborough United in the Championship.

However, after moving to Preston North End in 2022, he has played just 23 times in four years for the Lilywhites. His role, should he sign for the Foxes, would likely be further cover if Leicester’s rotten injury luck continued.

Why Do Leicester Need Another Goalkeeper?

While the East Midlands outfit have four goalkeepers on their books, only two are currently available for selection. Jakub Stolarczyk, who was their first-choice last term, was ruled out for the remainder of the campaign earlier this month after sustaining an ACL injury against Plymouth Argyle. Incidentally, he joins Ben Nelson as the second of Russell Martin’s squad to sustain a season-ending injury this term.

ADVERTISEMENT

A day before Stolarczyk’s diagnosis was revealed, Leicester allowed young goalkeeper Stevie Bausor to join Slough Town on a month-long loan. The 21-year-old, who joined his Polish teammate in coming through the Foxes academy, was named alongside Stolarczyk in the matchday squad for their Carabao Cup triumph over Northampton Town in the first game of the season.

Alex McCarthy, who reunited with his former Southampton boss Martin this summer, started the third-tier season as first-choice goalkeeper. He missed the success over the Cobblers with a knock, before starting the Foxes’ first two matches of the league season. However, Stolarczyk regained his spot for the League Cup defeat at Ipswich Town, retaining his place in the side for the stalemate at Milton Keynes Dons at the end of August.

ADVERTISEMENT

But there was yet more goalkeeping drama in the opening game of September, when the Polish shot-stopper was stretched off and replaced by the former Saints keeper. McCarthy has kept his place in the side since, though Leicester have conceded seven times in their past two matches against Oxford United and Stockport County. Franco Ravizzoli, also signed this summer, has appeared on the bench in those last two matches.

Next On The Chopping Block? - League One Preview
Welcome back to the League One Lowdown, where Sam takes the reins for a solo edition ahead of another action-packed EFL League One weekend! Kicking things off as the Game of the Week, high-flying Sheffield Wednesday host Stockport County at Hillsborough in a clash between two of the division's top-scoring sides. Wednesday average a home-high 2.8 goals per match, but they will face a stern test from a resilient Stockport team boasting strong away form, having scored seven goals across three away trips already this season.

Moving on to the Surprise of the Week, Sam examines whether Bromley can pull off an unexpected result against an unbeaten Huddersfield Town side. Despite Huddersfield’s impressive form, Bromley’s low block, physical style, and direct threats could frustrate the Terriers on a tight home pitch. The episode also highlights Three Things to Watch across the third tier.



First, a fierce rivalry unfolds as AFC Wimbledon host MK Dons, with MK Dons eager to turn their frequent draws into three points against a defensively stubborn Wimbledon side. Next, Luton Town travel to Bradford City in a fixture shrouded in headlines; Jack Wilshere looks to patch up a leaky Luton defense that has conceded 13 goals in six matches, while speculation swirls around whether Graham Alexander will remain at Bradford amidst rumors linking him to the open Preston North End job. Finally, Leyton Orient attempt to end an eight-game winless league home stretch against a set-piece dominant Stevenage side, making it a critical fixture for Richie Wellens to build momentum. The rest of the division offers fascinating narratives, including Burton Albion facing Mansfield Town, Barnsley hosting Leicester City, Blackpool taking on Plymouth Argyle, and Peterborough battling Doncaster Rovers. What are your thoughts on this weekend's matches? Leave your Game of the Week selections and three things to watch in the comments below, and don't forget to like, subscribe, hit the Hype button, and rate the show on audio platforms
